sections.h2: Where is Wise County, Virginia, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Wise County sits in the far southwest corner of Virginia, in the Appalachian coalfields along the Kentucky line. Wikipedia's county profile says it was formed in 1856 from Lee, Scott and Russell Counties and named for Governor Henry A. Wise. The county seat is the town of Wise, and the largest town is Big Stone Gap.

The county covers 405 square miles, nearly all of it land, and it lies in mountain country that includes High Knob and Powell Valley. Part of the Jefferson National Forest falls inside its borders. It touches Letcher, Pike and Harlan Counties in Kentucky, and Dickenson, Russell, Scott and Lee Counties in Virginia.

The independent city of Norton sits inside Wise County but is not part of it. For a house in Norton, ask the city's own offices, not the county offices described below.

sections.h2: What towns and communities make up Wise County?
sections.html:
Wise County has six incorporated towns: Appalachia, Big Stone Gap, Coeburn, Pound, St. Paul and Wise. The Census-designated places include Big Stone Gap East, Dunbar, East Stone Gap, Osaka, Riverview, Stonega and Tacoma, plus the campus of the University of Virginia's College at Wise.

Many sellers live in smaller unincorporated communities, such as Derby, Dooley, Exeter, Imboden, Inman, Pardee, Roda and Virginia City. A house in one of those places is taxed by the county only. A house inside a town may have town offices of its own, so ask the town hall what applies before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What shaped the Wise County economy?
sections.html:
Coal has been the defining industry in Wise County since the 1880s, when coal deposits became the dominant resource in the area. The Stonega Coke and Coal Company was formed in the town of Appalachia, and the work drew families from other states and from Europe.

The population peaked at 56,336 in the 1950 census and has fallen since, with a brief rise in the 1970s and 1980s. Today the county's employers include public ones. Red Onion State Prison (opened 1998) and Wallens Ridge State Prison (opened 1999) are both in the county, and Dominion Energy built the Virginia City Hybrid Energy Center there in 2012. The University of Virginia's College at Wise and Mountain Empire Community College in Big Stone Gap add education jobs.

For a seller, the practical point is that housing demand follows local jobs. A house that has sat empty after a family moved away or a parent passed is common, and our team buys houses in this condition as is.

sections.h2: What offices handle property tax in Wise County?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work: the Commissioner of the Revenue assesses real estate, and the Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Both are in the county seat of Wise.

The Commissioner's real estate department keeps the property records used for assessment and works with the Clerk of the Circuit Court and the Treasurer. Parcel details can be searched online through the county's EagleWeb Assessments tool. Railroads, pipelines and utility property are assessed by the State Corporation Commission or the Department of Taxation and then reported to the Commissioner.

sections.h2: What are the Wise County real estate tax rate and due dates?
sections.html:
For 2026 the Wise County real estate tax rate is $0.69 per $100 of assessed value, and bills are due on June 10 and November 10. The Board of Supervisors sets the rate each spring during budget talks.

As an illustration only, a house assessed at $100,000 would carry $690 of tax for the year at that rate, or $345 per half. Your own assessment will differ, so use the county parcel search for the real number.

  • Bills go to the owner on record as of January 1 and are mailed twice a year.
  • A 10% late penalty is added on June 11 and November 11.
  • Interest begins to accrue on July 1 and December 1, respectively.
  • A payment postmarked on or before June 10 or November 10 is accepted without penalty.
  • Not receiving a bill does not remove the penalty or interest.

If a mortgage company pays your tax, the county says it has sent them a request when your tax ticket notes it. Otherwise it is the owner's job to forward the bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Wise County assessment or correct an error?
sections.html:
Start with the Commissioner of the Revenue's office, which maintains the records and answers assessment questions. The county's real estate page links an FAQ on reassessments, so ask the office how often the county reassesses and when appeal windows fall for the current cycle. This page does not state those local dates.

State law gives one route for errors. Under Va. Code 58.1-3980, a person aggrieved by a local tax assessment may apply to the commissioner of the revenue for a correction within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later. For real estate, that route covers errors made by the commissioner or factual errors by others during a general reassessment.

The county also posts forms for land use assessment, tax relief for seniors and people with disabilities, disabled veterans, and surviving spouses of disabled veterans or of veterans killed in action. If you are selling a house that a surviving spouse has lived in, ask whether any relief was applied.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when I sell a house in Wise County?
sections.html:
Wise County bills the owner on record as of January 1, so a sale in the middle of the year does not by itself move the bill to the buyer. The closing statement is where the tax gets sorted out.

Ask the closing office to check these items with the Treasurer before you sign:

  • Whether the June 10 half has been paid, and whether the November 10 half is open.
  • Whether any 10% penalty or interest has been added to an unpaid half.
  • Who will pay the part of the year the buyer will own, since the bill follows the owner of record.
  • Whether the deed, will or list of heirs for an inherited house has been recorded, because the county uses Clerk of the Circuit Court records to update ownership.

The county asks owners to notify the Treasurer about any change of ownership or billing address. If you inherited a house with unpaid tax, we can often buy it as is and settle the balance from the sale. We make a written cash offer and you decide whether to accept it.

sections.h2: What should a Wise County seller know about schools, roads and daily life?
sections.html:
Buyers ask about commute and schools, so a seller gains from knowing the basics. Wise County Public Schools operates thirteen school facilities, and in 2011 the district consolidated six high schools into three: Union High in the west, Central High in the central and northern parts, and Eastside High in the east.

Major roads are U.S. Route 23, U.S. Route 58 Alternate, and State Routes 63, 72 and 83. Outdoor attractions include the High Knob area, the Clinch River and trails near the Appalachian Trail system.

Summer events include the Virginia-Kentucky District Fair in Wise and the outdoor drama The Trail of the Lonesome Pine in Big Stone Gap. None of that changes how a cash sale works, but it helps you describe the area when you talk to a buyer.

faqs.q: When are Wise County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Wise County real estate taxes are due on June 10 and November 10 each year. A 10% penalty is added the next day, and interest starts on July 1 and December 1.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 real estate tax rate in Wise County?
faqs.a: The 2026 rate is $0.69 per $100 of assessed value. The Board of Supervisors sets it in the spring during budget deliberations.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Wise County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's office bills and collects the tax. The Commissioner of the Revenue sets the assessment, and the bill goes to the owner on record as of January 1.

faqs.q: Is Norton part of Wise County for property tax?
faqs.a: No. Norton is an independent city that sits inside the county's borders but is not part of the county, so ask the city about its houses.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Wise County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax carries a 10% penalty and interest, and it should be paid or settled at closing. Call the Treasurer for the exact balance and ask your closing office how it will be handled.
